name: United States
tagline: Four years, no fixed major on day one, and the widest price range on earth
summary: An American bachelor's degree takes four years and starts broad: you take courses across several fields and usually declare a major at the end of year two. Admission is 'holistic' - your grades matter most, but so do essays, teacher references, what you do outside school, and increasingly again the SAT or ACT. As a Danish student you are an international applicant everywhere, so you pay the published sticker price unless a university gives you financial aid, and only a handful of universities give internationals enough aid to make it affordable. The cost range is enormous: from roughly 40,000 USD a year at a public university to over 95,000 USD a year at a private one.
whyConsider: You do not have to choose your subject before you arrive - you can start in autumn 2027 and declare a major in 2029.
A small group of very wealthy private universities and liberal arts colleges will meet 100% of your assessed financial need, including flights, no matter what your family earns.
Good HL results often convert into real course credit, which can let you skip introductory courses or even finish early.
Liberal arts colleges are small (1,500-2,500 students), taught by professors rather than teaching assistants, and are often more generous to internationals than the famous research universities.
Research, internships and campus jobs are built into the undergraduate experience in a way that is rare in Europe.
watchOuts: Sticker price. Harvard's published billed cost for 2025-26 was 86,926 USD for one year, and that is before health insurance and flights.
Most universities are need-aware for internationals: asking for money reduces your chance of getting in. Only a very short list is need-blind for non-Americans.
The testing landscape flipped back. Harvard and Yale both require the SAT or ACT again for autumn 2027 entry, and IB results do not substitute for the test at Yale.

Deadlines are brutally early: Early Action and Early Decision close 1 November 2026, most Regular Decision 1 January 2027, and the University of California closes 30 November 2026 - all long before you sit your IB exams.
Immigration costs and admin are real: I-20, SEVIS fee, embassy interview, and post-study work depends on an OPT approval you cannot count on.

ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: There is no national minimum. Selective universities look at the whole transcript and at HL subject choice rather than at a points threshold. Higher Level subjects are what earn credit; Standard Level rarely does.
ibRecognition.gradeConversion: There is no national IB-to-GPA conversion. Each university reads your IB predicted grades and, later, your final July results directly. The University of California publishes a credit conversion: a full IB Diploma with 30+ points earns 6 quarter units, and each Higher Level exam graded 5, 6 or 7 earns 8 quarter units (5.3 semester units), usually 24 quarter units in total.
notes: Credit for HL 5+ is common but the rules differ at every single university - check the specific university's IB credit page, not a general guide.
Yale states that IB results may be added to an application but cannot replace the required SAT or ACT score.
Harvard will accept IB scores instead of the SAT/ACT only where testing is genuinely unavailable, not as a normal alternative.
Your school sends predicted grades; final results arrive 6 July 2027, well after decisions. Offers are effectively made on predictions plus everything else in the file.

portal.name: Three application environments, not one: the Common App, the University of California application, and institutions that take only their own

deadlines.label: Common App opens for the cycle
deadlines.notes: The rounds, the per-college dates and the evidence are on the Common App Application Route. The cited post is dated 31 July 2026 and announces the opening of the 2026-27 season, which is the season that leads to entry in autumn 2027; it was re-read and still carried that date on 23 September 2026.

deadlines.label: Applications close — and there is no American closing date, because no American body sets one
deadlines.notes: This is the headline entry for the United States and it deliberately carries no date, because a single American deadline does not exist. There is no ministry, no clearing house and no national closing day; every college sets its own, and four different rounds run on four different promises. The shape, from the institutions recorded on this site and re-read on 23 September 2026: Early Action, Restrictive Early Action and Single-Choice Early Action all close 1 November 2026 (Harvard, Stanford, Yale, Illinois, Macalester) and are not binding. Early Decision I closes somewhere between 1 and 15 November 2026 — Macalester 1 November, Amherst 9 November, Bowdoin and Grinnell 15 November — and is binding; see the next entry. Early Decision II closes in early January 2027 — Macalester 1 January, Bowdoin and Grinnell 5 January — and is also binding. Regular Decision closes between 1 and 15 January 2027 — Harvard 1 January, Yale 2 January, Stanford, Amherst and Illinois 5 January, MIT 4 January, Grinnell and Macalester 15 January. The University of California is earlier than all of them and has its own entry below. After a college's own Regular Decision date that college is finished for the year: there is no Clearing, no late round and no second intake. Write each college's own date into your own calendar and do not carry one college's date to another.

deadlines.label: Early Decision is binding — applying early is a commitment, not an early submission
deadlines.audience: anyone considering an Early Decision application
deadlines.notes: This entry carries no date on purpose: the thing you need to know about Early Decision is not when it closes but what signing it costs you. Early Decision I (1 to 15 November 2026) and Early Decision II (early January 2027) are binding in the strongest sense the American system has. Amherst's wording is that you agree not to be an Early Decision candidate anywhere else and, if admitted, to withdraw your applications from every other college and enrol. It is a signed agreement — student, parent and school counsellor — filed inside the Common App for one college only. Two consequences follow and neither is obvious from a calendar. First, an admitted Early Decision applicant does not get the 1 May reply date: that decision was made in November. Second, and for a Danish family paying from abroad this is usually the more expensive loss, you can never compare financial aid offers, because you will only ever hold one. Early Action, Restrictive Early Action and Single-Choice Early Action are NOT binding — you keep every offer and still reply on 1 May — but Stanford's and Yale's restrict where else you may apply early, so they still decide your whole autumn in October. Missing an early round costs you that round's higher admit rate; signing an Early Decision agreement costs you the choice.

deadlines.label: SAT, registration closes for the 7 November 2026 sitting
deadlines.audience: applicants to colleges that require the SAT or ACT
deadlines.notes: The College Board's own dates page states that "These test dates and deadlines apply to all students—U.S. and international—taking the SAT", so a Copenhagen test centre runs the same calendar as an American one. This is the last sitting that can realistically reach a college which allows November scores into an early round; it is already after the 1 November early deadlines, so check each college's own policy on late-arriving scores before relying on it. Whether you need a test at all is a per-college question with no national answer: Yale, Harvard, Stanford and MIT require the SAT or ACT for autumn 2027 entry, and Yale states that IB results may accompany the test but not replace it; NYU, Michigan, Illinois and Amherst are test-optional. No ACT date is recorded on this site: act.org's registration page served only 2024 test dates and its test-dates URL returned HTTP 404 when both were read on 23 September 2026, so the 2026-27 ACT calendar could not be established. If your colleges accept the ACT, take its dates from act.org directly and do not assume they match the SAT's.

deadlines.label: SAT, registration closes for the 5 December 2026 sitting — the last SAT that reaches a January deadline
deadlines.audience: applicants to colleges that require the SAT or ACT
deadlines.notes: 5 December 2026 is the final SAT sitting of the 2026-27 calendar before Regular Decision closes; the next one is 6 March 2027, by which time every Regular Decision file in this cycle has been read. If a college on your list requires the test, this registration date is the real end of the line, not the December sitting itself. The remaining 2026-27 sittings after it — 6 March, 1 May and 5 June 2027 — are recorded here only so that nobody mistakes them for a second chance at admission; they are of use for a gap year or a transfer, not for autumn 2027 entry.

deadlines.label: University of California application closes
deadlines.notes: The cited page gives "November 1 - 30" as the "Fall 2027 admission application filing period", and the application itself opens on 1 August. It is the earliest deadline on the American list and there is no second round and no early round — the University of California runs neither Early Action nor Early Decision, does not read letters of recommendation, and asks four 350-word personal insight questions instead of the Common App essay. The University of California's three later dates — the 1 May reply, the 1 July final transcript and the 15 July IB results deadline — are each recorded as their own entry below rather than left in this note.

deadlines.label: MIT, financial aid documents for Early Action applicants
deadlines.audience: applicants asking MIT for need-based aid
deadlines.notes: Published on MIT's deadlines page as "November 30" with no calendar year, as every date on that page is; the year here is read into the 2026-27 cycle that leads to autumn 2027 entry, which is why this entry is marked provisional. It falls a month after the 1 November Early Action application itself, so it is a date that is easy to miss precisely because the application is already in. Promoted out of the note on the financial aid entry below so that it can be sorted, counted and shown on a calendar.

deadlines.label: MIT, financial aid documents for Regular Action applicants
deadlines.audience: applicants asking MIT for need-based aid
deadlines.notes: Published on MIT's deadlines page as "February 15" with no calendar year; the year here is read into the cycle this profile covers, hence provisional. MIT's Regular Action application closes on 4 January, so the aid papers are due six weeks after the application — long enough to forget about. Promoted out of the note on the financial aid entry below so that it can be sorted, counted and shown on a calendar.

deadlines.label: Financial aid forms are due with the application, not after it — and the FAFSA is not the form you file
deadlines.notes: Each institution's aid deadline is its own, and at most of them it is the application deadline itself. Grinnell states that "All financial aid forms must be submitted by the same deadline as the Common Application". Macalester states that "financial aid cannot be awarded after an offer of admission has been made, nor at any time during their studies at Macalester" — that is a door that closes permanently, not a late penalty. Bowdoin's Regular Decision aid deadline is 1 February, a month after its application date. MIT's two aid dates, 30 November and 15 February, now have entries of their own above. A family that applies first and asks about money in the spring has forfeited the money. Which form: as a Danish citizen you file the CSS Profile, not the FAFSA. The FAFSA is the United States federal aid application and federal aid requires US citizenship or eligible-non-citizen status, which an F-1 student visa is not — so every FAFSA date you will meet on American admissions pages, including the 1 October opening and the 2 March deadline printed on the University of California's own dates page, is not yours. Grinnell asks for "the 2027-28 CSS Profile"; Macalester asks for the CSS Profile "OR the 2027-2028 International Student Application for Financial Assistance (ISAFA)" and points international applicants who cannot afford the CSS Profile fee at the free ISAFA instead, because neither college waives the CSS Profile fee for international applicants. The CSS Profile itself carries no national deadline — the colleges set them, typically 1 or 15 November for the early rounds and January to February for Regular Decision. Its opening date for 2027-28 could not be established from the College Board: cssprofile.collegeboard.org offered only a "Fall 2027/Spring 2028" sign-in with no opening date when read on 23 September 2026, the student-guide PDF could not be parsed, and profile.collegeboard.org returned HTTP 502. The customary opening is 1 October of the preceding year, and the most recent stated instance found on an official page is Cornell's "The 2026-27 FAFSA form opens October 1, 2025" — which is the previous cycle and about the wrong form, so nothing has been inferred from it here. Open the CSS Profile in early October 2026 and check the date yourself.

deadlines.label: Reply deadline — the national candidates' reply date
deadlines.notes: The one date in the American calendar that every institution shares, and the only national one on this page. Until 1 May 2027 you may hold every offer you have and compare the aid figures; after it, the offer you have not replied to is gone, and your place goes to somebody on a waiting list. The University of California states it with its year attached — "Deadline for all fall 2027 admitted first-year students to submit their SIR" — and calls it the Statement of Intent to Register; MIT, Harvard, Stanford, Illinois and the Common App colleges call it the reply date and publish it as a bare "May 1". An Early Decision admission is the exception: that choice was made in November and this date does not belong to you. A source note for whoever re-checks this: this entry previously cited only amherst.edu, which returns HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed to automated retrieval and so can never be confirmed by an automated verifier. Amherst is kept in the source list because it is the page that states the date with a full calendar year for a Common App college, but the primary source has been moved to the University of California's dates page, which carries the claim, carries the year and can be fetched.

deadlines.label: University of California, final official transcript due
deadlines.audience: applicants who have accepted a University of California offer
deadlines.notes: Published as "Final, official transcripts must be postmarked or electronically submitted". This is a condition of an offer you have already accepted, so missing it costs the place rather than the application. Your gymnasium sends it, not you, and a Danish school in the first week of July is a quieter place than it is in June — ask for it before the summer. Promoted out of the note on the University of California entry above, where it was described only as "the July results deadline".

deadlines.label: IB results released
deadlines.notes: Every American decision in this cycle is made before this date, on predicted grades, a school report and everything else in the file — which is the whole shape of an American application and the reason the calendar above stops in May. What each college does if your actual results fall short of the predictions is set by that college and is not established here; ask before you accept. The date is inferred rather than cited, and both the inference and the reason it could not be checked are held once, in data/ib-calendar.json with the Evidence record ev-ib-results-day-2027-05. It is marked provisional here for that reason. The IB result that does have a hard American consequence is not this one — it is the University of California's 15 July deadline nine days later, which is the entry below.

deadlines.label: University of California, official IB examination results due
deadlines.audience: IB candidates who have accepted a University of California offer
deadlines.notes: Published as "Deadline for official AP and IB examination results to be postmarked or electronically submitted". This is the single most IB-specific deadline in the United States and it is the tightest: results are released on about 6 July 2027 and the University of California wants them, officially, nine days later. You request the transmission from the IB yourself, through candidate results services — it is not automatic and the university will not chase it. Promoted out of the University of California entry above, where it appeared only as the phrase "the July results deadline" with no date attached.

deadlines.label: Rolling-admission priority date, Arizona State University
deadlines.notes: Arizona State is the one institution on this site that does not run a selection tournament: it publishes priority dates rather than closing dates and admits on a rolling basis against published criteria. When its international first-year page was read on 23 September 2026 it carried only fall 2026 (15 January 2026) and spring 2027 (1 November 2026), and nothing has been inferred for fall 2027 from either. The most recent actual fall priority date is therefore 15 January 2026, recorded here as precedent and not as a prediction. Recheck from about December 2026.

steps: From spring 2026, build a list of 8-12 institutions in three groups: places that meet full need for internationals, places likely to give you merit money, and one or two you could genuinely afford at full price.

Work out which of the three application environments each one sits in. Twelve of the fourteen here are on the Common App; Berkeley is on the University of California application and closes a month earlier; MIT takes only its own.
Register for and sit the SAT or ACT in 2026 if any institution on your list requires it, and plan a retake date before November. Yale and MIT require it and do not accept the IB instead.
Create a Common App account when it opens on 31 July 2026, fill in your personal details once, and add your institutions.

Ask two teachers and your studievejleder for references in spring 2026, not in October. Your counsellor also uploads the school report and your predicted IB grades - Illinois wants those a week after the application itself.
Write the 650-word personal essay over the summer, then the supplemental essays. The University of California asks four 350-word personal insight questions instead and needs writing of its own.
File the University of California application between 1 and 30 November 2026. It is the earliest deadline on the list and there is no second round.

Submit early-round applications - 1 November for Early Action almost everywhere, between 1 and 15 November for Early Decision depending on the college - then the Regular Decision applications between 1 and 15 January 2027.
Submit financial aid forms by the same deadline as the application, not later. Macalester states that aid cannot be awarded after an offer of admission is made.
Decide by 1 May 2027, then wait for the I-20, pay the 350 USD SEVIS fee and book an embassy appointment in Copenhagen for the F-1 visa.
Arrange the compulsory student health insurance, or a waiver, before the July deadline. In Massachusetts it is required by state law.
application.selectionNotes: Holistic review at most institutions: no published points threshold, no ranking table, no guaranteed entry. Committees read grades and the rigour of your subjects first, then essays, references, activities and context, and at many institutions also your ability to pay. Early Decision is binding - Amherst's wording is that you agree to withdraw your applications from other colleges and enrol - and it meaningfully raises your odds, but it removes your ability to compare financial aid offers. Early Action and Restrictive Early Action are not binding, though Stanford's and Yale's restrict where else you may apply early. The University of California does not run any early round at all, does not read letters of recommendation, and asks four short personal insight questions instead of an essay. Arizona State does not run a tournament at all: it admits against published criteria on a rolling basis. International admit rates at the most famous universities are in the low single digits; do not build a list out of them.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: Everything. The question is not whether the degree is in English but whether you must prove your English.
language.englishProof: Many universities waive TOEFL/IELTS for students who have been taught in English, which an IB Diploma from an English-medium programme normally demonstrates - but the waiver is not automatic and each university sets its own rule. Check the specific university; where no waiver applies, typical requirements are TOEFL iBT 100+ or IELTS 7.0+ at selective universities. The exact thresholds were not verified for this guide.
notes: Your IB English A Literature or Language and Literature result is the strongest evidence you can offer, but ask each admissions office in writing whether it replaces the test.
Some universities also use the Duolingo English Test. Availability varies year to year.

tuitionEuEea.value: Not applicable - the United States does not have an EU/EEA fee category. As a Dane you pay the international or out-of-state rate everywhere.

tuitionNonEu.value: Private universities: Harvard's published billed cost for 2025-26 was 86,926 USD (tuition 59,320, fees 5,476, housing 13,532, food 8,598), with total billed and unbilled costs of 90,426-95,426 USD plus 4,308 USD health insurance if you are not covered elsewhere. Public universities: UC Berkeley's 2026-27 tuition and fees for a new student are 18,214 USD, but new out-of-state students pay an additional Nonresident Supplemental Tuition of 39,270 USD, so an international first-year pays roughly 57,500 USD in tuition and fees and a total cost of attendance around 94,000 USD in a residence hall.

costs.applicationFee: Harvard 95 USD; University of California 95 USD per campus for international applicants (80 USD for domestic). Most universities charge 50-100 USD per application, and fee waivers exist but are usually aimed at low-income US students.

livingCostMonthly.value: Not published as a monthly figure. American universities publish an annual 'cost of attendance' that already includes housing, food, books, transport and personal expenses - see the tuition figures above. UC Berkeley's 2026-27 estimate for housing and utilities in an off-campus apartment is 14,386 USD for a nine-month academic year, about 1,609 USD a month.

notes: Always read the 'cost of attendance', never the tuition line alone. The COA is also the number financial aid is calculated against.
Health insurance is compulsory and charged separately at most universities. Harvard's was 4,308 USD for 2025-26.
Budget for flights home twice a year; Berkeley allows 0-5,000 USD for transportation and Harvard allows the same range.
The I-901 SEVIS fee is 350 USD for F-1 students, paid before your visa interview.

NOT VERIFIED ON AN OFFICIAL PAGE: the nonimmigrant visa application (MRV) fee is widely reported as 185 USD and a new 250 USD Visa Integrity Fee was introduced by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act with effect from 1 October 2025. We could not fetch travel.state.gov to confirm either figure - check current fees at travel.state.gov before you budget.

funding: Need-based institutional aid. A short list of universities is need-blind for international applicants and meets 100% of assessed need. Harvard states plainly that international students are eligible for exactly the same aid as Americans, that admission is need-blind, and that families earning under 100,000 USD pay nothing, while families up to 200,000 USD have tuition covered. NOT FULLY VERIFIED: widely reported members of this group also include Yale, Princeton, MIT, Amherst, Bowdoin, Dartmouth, Brown, Notre Dame and Washington and Lee - confirm on each university's own financial aid page before you apply.

Need-aware full-need aid. Many strong liberal arts colleges consider your finances when deciding but then meet 100% of need if they admit you. Grinnell College is explicit about this: need-aware for internationals, then 100% of institutionally determined need met.

Merit scholarships. Some universities award merit money regardless of need - Grinnell says outstanding international applicants are considered for merit aid whether or not they apply for need-based help. Merit awards are usually partial, 10,000-30,000 USD a year, and are concentrated at universities outside the top 20.

Athletic scholarships (NCAA). Real but narrow. Division I and II programmes can offer athletic money; Division III, which includes most liberal arts colleges, cannot offer any athletic aid at all. You must register with the NCAA Eligibility Center and be recruited by a coach - you cannot apply for an athletic scholarship the way you apply for a grant. For a Danish IB student this is realistic only in sports where you already compete at national level, typically rowing, swimming, football, handball, golf or tennis.

Danish SU. Danish state education support can in some circumstances follow you abroad for a full degree. Rules are set by Uddannelses- og Forskningsstyrelsen and were not verified for this guide - talk to your studievejleder and check su.dk early, because the application has its own deadlines.
US federal student loans are not available to international students, and most private US loans require a US co-signer.
workRights: On an F-1 visa you may work on campus during your studies, subject to limits set by your university, and off-campus work generally requires prior authorisation. After your degree, Optional Practical Training (OPT) gives up to 12 months of work authorisation directly related to your major, and graduates of approved STEM degrees can apply for a further 24-month extension if the employer is enrolled in E-Verify. You cannot start OPT until USCIS approves Form I-765 and you receive the Employment Authorization Document. Source: https://www.uscis.gov/working-in-the-united-states/students-and-exchange-visitors/optional-practical-training-opt-for-f-1-students
residency: There is no EU-style free movement. After you accept an offer the university issues Form I-20, you pay the I-901 SEVIS fee of 350 USD, complete the DS-160 form, pay the visa fee and attend an interview at the US Embassy in Copenhagen for an F-1 student visa. Bring the SEVIS receipt to the interview - it is required. You may enter the US up to 30 days before your programme starts. Sources: https://www.ice.gov/sevis/i901 and https://studyinthestates.dhs.gov/students/prepare/paying-the-i-901-sevis-fee
housing: Almost all universities house first-year students on campus and many require it. That is a genuine advantage over Europe: you do not hunt for a room, you get assigned one, and the cost is in the published cost of attendance. Harvard's 2025-26 housing and food came to 22,130 USD; Berkeley's residence hall housing and meal plan for 2026-27 are 16,640 USD and 7,000 USD. From year two, many students move off campus, which is where costs and hassle rise - Berkeley budgets 14,386 USD for nine months in an off-campus apartment.
healthcare: Health insurance is compulsory and expensive, and the Danish yellow card and EHIC are worthless in the US. Universities charge their own student health plan unless you can prove equivalent cover - Harvard's was 4,308 USD for 2025-26 and Berkeley's SHIP is 5,066 USD for 2026-27. Private Danish travel or study insurance sometimes qualifies for a waiver, but the university decides and the waiver deadline is usually 1 July. Assume you will pay for the university plan.

institutions.name: Harvard University
institutions.englishBachelors: Four-year AB or SB; you declare a concentration in the second year.
institutions.note: Need-blind for internationals and meets 100% of need, which makes it one of the few places where a Danish family on a normal income could actually afford to send a child - but the admit rate is in the low single digits, so treat it as a lottery ticket, not a plan.

institutions.name: Yale University
institutions.englishBachelors: Four-year BA or BS across roughly 80 majors, with a strong residential college system.
institutions.note: Requires the SAT or ACT from every first-year applicant and states explicitly that IB results cannot replace it - so if Yale is on your list, book a test date in 2026.

institutions.name: Massachusetts Institute of Technology
institutions.englishBachelors: Four-year SB degrees; everyone takes the same science and maths core in year one.
institutions.note: The only institution in this profile that has never joined the Common App: you apply through MIT's own portal, Early Action closes 1 November and Regular Action 4 January, not 1 January. The SAT or ACT is required and there is no IB alternative. Its IB credit rule is the narrowest we found anywhere in the United States - Higher Level only, grade 7 only, and nothing at all for IB Biology, Chemistry or Information Technology in a Global Society.

institutions.name: Stanford University
institutions.englishBachelors: Four-year BA/BS on a quarter system, so you take more, shorter courses than at most US universities.
institutions.note: Reported to have reinstated a testing requirement and to be need-aware for internationals - check both on Stanford's own pages, as we could not verify them.

institutions.name: Amherst College
institutions.englishBachelors: Four-year BA with an open curriculum - no distribution requirements at all beyond your major.
institutions.note: About 1,900 students and consistently named as one of the very few liberal arts colleges that is need-blind for international applicants and meets full need; it is as selective as an Ivy, so apply alongside, not instead of, less selective colleges.

institutions.name: Bowdoin College
institutions.englishBachelors: Four-year BA, about 1,800 students, small classes and no graduate students competing for attention.
institutions.note: Regularly listed among the need-blind, full-need colleges for internationals; coastal Maine is beautiful and genuinely remote, which suits some Danish students and not others.

institutions.name: Grinnell College
institutions.englishBachelors: Four-year BA with an individually advised curriculum; roughly 1,700 students and an unusually high international share.
institutions.note: One of the most realistic targets on this list: need-aware for internationals but then meets 100% of assessed need, and also considers internationals for merit awards. ED I 15 November, ED II 5 January, RD 15 January - aid forms due the same day.

institutions.name: Macalester College
institutions.englishBachelors: Four-year BA with an explicit internationalist mission; around 2,000 students in a real city.
institutions.note: Long-standing reputation for recruiting and funding international students, and being in the Twin Cities means jobs, flights and a Scandinavian-heavy Midwest that feels less foreign than you would expect. Confirm its current international aid policy directly.

institutions.name: Colby College
institutions.englishBachelors: Four-year BA, about 2,200 students, with a January term for one intensive project.
institutions.note: Reported to award substantial credit for a strong full IB Diploma - worth asking the registrar directly, because a year of credit changes the total cost of the degree more than any scholarship will.

institutions.name: New York University
institutions.englishBachelors: Four-year degrees across separate schools - you apply to one school, such as Stern or Tisch, not to NYU in general.
institutions.note: Enormous international intake and campuses in Abu Dhabi and Shanghai, but it is famously need-aware and does not meet full need for most internationals; go in expecting to pay a large share of a very high New York cost of living.

institutions.name: University of Michigan-Ann Arbor
institutions.englishBachelors: Four-year degrees across 19 schools, with a large liberal arts college at the centre.
institutions.note: A top-tier public university with a classic American campus experience; out-of-state and international tuition is close to private-university levels and institutional aid for internationals is limited.

institutions.name: University of California, Berkeley
institutions.englishBachelors: Four-year BA/BS; you apply to a college within Berkeley, and some majors are capped.
institutions.note: Apply through the UC application by 30 November 2026, not the Common App. For 2026-27 a new international pays 18,214 USD of tuition and fees plus 39,270 USD Nonresident Supplemental Tuition, and UC gives essentially no need-based aid to internationals - but the UC system's published IB credit rules are the most generous and transparent in the country.

institutions.name: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
institutions.englishBachelors: Four-year degrees; you apply to a specific major, and engineering and computer science are far harder to enter than the university overall.
institutions.note: A serious engineering and computing school at a public-university price, with a huge international community and a less theatrical admissions process than the private universities.

institutions.name: Arizona State University
institutions.englishBachelors: Four-year degrees across more than 350 undergraduate programmes, with published admission criteria rather than holistic review.
institutions.note: The counterweight to a list of single-digit admit rates: ASU admits against published criteria rather than by tournament, decides on a rolling basis, and accepts either its own application or the Common App with no stated preference. The application fee for an international applicant is 90 USD. Its priority date for fall 2027 is not published yet, and it states an English-proficiency requirement without naming an IB exemption - ask in writing whether your English A or B Higher Level result covers it.
